pr.title: Fill a review placeholder that sits alone in backticks
pr.head: b7a34e805e9d0a1d1b9fa56380bb1d3f9f82a9f7

summary: When a review agent publishes a review, it writes the body to a file and runs project review publish. That command fills a few placeholders in the body: {census} becomes the count of finding threads, {took} the review's duration, {seconds} the same span in seconds, and {sha} and {short_sha} the head commit. Until this change, it filled them only in prose. Any code in backticks went out exactly as written, so a review could quote code that happens to contain braces.

Agents often want the SHA in code font, so they wrap the placeholder in backticks. That span counted as quoted code, and review loops published dozens of reviews that showed a literal placeholder on GitHub instead of the SHA.

This change fills an inline code span whose whole content is one placeholder, and keeps the backticks around the value. A placeholder inside longer code, and everything in a fenced block, still go out as written. A lone census span now also satisfies the check that a body prints the census. To mention a placeholder by name, a review quotes it inside longer code, such as print({census}).

groups.title: Filling lone placeholder spans
groups.kicker: The rule change in compose, which builds the posted review text
intro: compose in src/projector/review.py turns the agent's body file into the review text that GitHub receives. It finds quoted code with the CODE pattern, which matches a fenced block or a single-backtick inline span, and fills placeholders only in the prose between those matches.

The change adds LONE_PLACEHOLDER, a pattern for an inline span that holds exactly one placeholder. Two places use it: the census check, which now keeps such spans when it looks for {census}, and the fill loop, which replaces such a span with the value wrapped in backticks.

files.note: Adds LONE_PLACEHOLDER and uses it in the census check and the fill loop of compose.

checks.text: CODE matches a fenced block as one piece, so LONE_PLACEHOLDER.fullmatch can match only a single-backtick span. A probe against compose at this head refused a body whose only census sat inside a fenced block.

The census check drops all code except lone spans. Removing the old PLACEHOLDER.search test loses nothing, because a body that holds {census} already holds a placeholder. A census quoted inside longer code is still refused, as the updated test checks.

compose is the only reader of PLACEHOLDER, CODE, and LONE_PLACEHOLDER, and none of the filled values contains a backtick that could break the span. A probe filled a SHA wrapped in double backticks and a lone census span as expected.

groups.title: Tests for the new rule
groups.kicker: A new test for lone spans, and two tests moved off the old behavior
intro: The new test publishes a body that uses lone spans for the short SHA, the full SHA, the duration, and the census, plus a fenced block that holds a placeholder. It checks that each span shows its value in backticks and that the fenced block stays literal.

Two existing tests relied on a lone span staying literal. The census refusal test now quotes the census inside print(...), and the test for code that mentions braces quotes the short-SHA placeholder inside longer code.

checks.text: The full suite passes at this head: 455 tests with one skip, the compiled-site check that needs npm ci in site/.

files.note: Adds test_a_span_holding_only_a_placeholder_is_filled_in_code_font and updates two tests that pinned the old literal behavior.

groups.title: Documentation of the rule
groups.kicker: The review skill and the CLI reference describe which spans publish fills
intro: Review agents read skills/review-pr/SKILL.md to learn how to write a body, and docs/cli.md is the command reference. Both now say that publish fills placeholders in prose and in a span that holds one placeholder alone, but not in longer quoted code or fenced blocks.
